news.title: ’Time for another voice’: Diallo launches campaign to dethrone Fifa boss Infantino
news.lede: Philippe Diallo, head of the French Football Federation, on Tuesday officially launched his campaign to replace Gianni Infantino as president of the game's world ruling body Fifa with a call for change – following a series of scandals that threatened to tear apart the 122-year-old organisation. “The values of our sport have been trampled on," said Diallo, moments after receiving the backing of the French Football Federation (FFF) for his candidacy to end Infantino's 11-year reign. “Within a democratic process, it is time for another voice to be heard, one that is more respectful of football." In September, the FFF withdrew its support for Infantino's bid for a fourth term, following a string of controversies during and after the 2026 World Cup held this summer in the United States, Mexico and Canada.

news.title: Clear challenge: Spanish federation sends fiery message to Morocco over 2030 World Cup final
news.lede: The Spanish Football Federation has sent a strong message to Morocco concerning the bid to host the final of the 2030 World Cup.The battle between Morocco and Spain to stage the 2030 World Cup final has intensified after recent moves by both sides, and major developments look likely in the coming months.Morocco, Spain and Portugal are co-hosting the 2030 World Cup. Who gets the final, though, is a fierce contest.Morocco's Hassan II Stadium is one of the leading candidates. With a planned capacity of around 115,000, it would become the largest football stadium in the world when it opens, as expected, in 2029. Naturally, each country is doing everything it can to host the most important match in the world.Spain are desperate to host the final at either the Santiago Bernabéu or Camp Nou.

news.title: France coach praises development of Saudi football
news.lede: José Alcocer, the head coach of the France U17 national team, praised the progress Saudi Arabian football has made in recent years ahead of the FIFA World Cup for youth in Qatar. The tournament will take place from November 19 to December 13, featuring Saudi Arabia in Group D alongside France, Uruguay, and Haiti. The Saudi Arabia U-20 team will begin their journey against Uruguay on November 19, followed by a match against France on the 22nd of the same month, before concluding the group stage with a game against Haiti on November 25. Alkhosir stated in remarks to the official website of the FIFA World Cup: "Saudi Arabia has been doing a great job for a long time, and it has made significant progress."

news.title: Islander leads England into World Cup last 16 after topping group
news.lede: ‘To get a clean sheet heading into the round of 16 feels good’. Those were the words of Manx footballer Sean Jackson after captaining England to the top of their group at the World Amputee Football Federation (WAFF) World Cup in Mexico. The former Isle of Man goalkeeper and Marown, Laxey and St George’s player helped his country secure two wins and a draw from their opening three matches to finish top of Group F. England will now face Egypt in the last 16 on Wednesday (November 18), with kick-off at 10.30pm UK time, after an impressive end to the group stage.

news.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
news.lede: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation. “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina.

news.title: Infantino challenger Diallo: Football needs a more 'respectful voice'
news.lede: FIFA presidential candidate Philippe Diallo says football's values have been "trampled underfoot" by incumbent Gianni Infantino as he set out his stall ahead of March's election. European governing body UEFA announced on Monday that French Football Federation (FFF) chief Diallo would be its candidate to try to stop Infantino winning a fourth term at the top of the global game.
